subject: Labels overlapping when faceting and specifying range

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Labels overlapping when faceting and specifying range
parts:
Hey everyone,
I am having trouble making my plots look nice when I use `facet_grid` along with `coord_cartesian` to specify the y limits. The labels overlap.

For example,
library(ggplot2)
# Data to plot
df <- data.frame(A = 1:6, B = 1:6, F = rep(c("H", "L"), times = 3))
# Default case. The axis labels for the H and L facets 2 and 6, respectively, do not overlap.
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = A, y = B)) + geom_point() + facet_grid(F ~ .)
# Using ylim, things continue to look good. There is a bit of spacing below the 0 in H and 5 and L
# so that they don't overlap.
p + ylim(0, 5)
# But I don't want to subset the data, I want to zoom in. In this example it does not matter, but
# my real data is much different. To do this I need to use coord_cartesian...
p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5))
# As you can see, none of that nice spacing between the values and the border exist anymore so the 0 and 5
# sit directly on top of each other.
# I tried using `pretty` breaks but that did not help either.
p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty)

Any suggestions?

Many thanks,
Doug

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Labels overlapping when faceting and specifying range
parts:
Hi:

Does this work for you?

p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty) +
theme(panel.margin = grid::unit(0.4, "cm"))

Dennis

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Labels overlapping when faceting and specifying range
parts:
Hey Dennis,
Thanks very much. I can play around with that and get it to work.

At a higher level though, I am still not sure why one needs to adjust the panel margins like this. I understand the difference in subsetting vs. zooming using ylim vs. coord_cartesian, respectively, but at the end of the day all you are doing in either case is changing the range of an axis. I think you should expect the same plot output regardless of whether you are subsetting or zooming. Do folks agree? Should this be a feature request (or a bug fix, depending on how you look at it)? Or am I just missing the boat here?

Best wishes,
Doug
